purpose: Deep research synthesis: what agents really want/need and which AgentPress features target those painpoints.

wants.evidence: MCP/code-execution patterns reduce token overhead; agents need compact tool cards and routing, not huge catalogs in-context.
wants.feature: tool routing decision matrix + compact connector cards
wants.acceptance: agent can choose one tool/connector without loading full docs

wants.evidence: MCP/enterprise connector docs emphasize endpoint/auth/authorization metadata and remote/local deployment modes.
wants.feature: MCP connector auth readiness + permission handshake
wants.acceptance: connector declares auth mode, scopes, no-secret dry run, approval gate

wants.evidence: LLMOps/agent eval tooling focuses on traces, task completion, debugging, monitoring, and regression checks.
wants.acceptance: runs emit trace refs, eval score, task completion, failure taxonomy

wants.evidence: agents/operators need package, registry, remote endpoint, and local stdio install routes before using connectors.
wants.acceptance: each connector has install/deploy mode and publish blocker

wants.evidence: coding agents need approval/reviewer/security gates before file writes, releases, messages, payments, credentials.
wants.feature: approval/reviewer gates already built; add connector permission handoff
wants.acceptance: connector declares R-level and approval_ref requirement

wants.evidence: Cline/Roo/OpenHands comparisons center workflow differences; users need persona/native quickstarts and host transcripts.
wants.feature: persona quickstarts + host transcript dropbox already built; add first-run checklist per connector
wants.acceptance: each connector has exact first-run command + evidence output
